Finally, we have:

$$\begin{array}{c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c}
 && A B C D _b  \\ 
&+& B C D A _b  \\ 
\cline{2-6} 
&E F G H I _b. \\ 
\end{array}$$

In base $b$, each letter represents a different digit not between $0$ and $a-1$, which are $9$ to $15$ respectively.

Here $E = 2+A$, which is $9$ times $b$ or $9b$. But $E$ is a single digit, so we know that $b < 16$.

$F$ is unknown, but $F = 3AB$ is always even, so $b$ must be odd.

$I$ can neither be $2$ nor $3$, so $b$ must be $5$, $7$, $11$, or $13$.

Here we have:

$$\begin{array}{c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c}
 && A & B & C & 9 _{5} \\ 
&+& B & C & 9 & A _{5} \\ 
\cline{2-6} 
&0 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 2 _{5}. \\ 
\end{array}$$

Now, we know that $0$ must be $D + 2$ or $6$, for $15b$. Hence $A \neq 3$ or $5$, so $A$ can be $1$ or $7$. But $0$ can never be the last half of something like $E$, so from $0$ is no other than $D + 2$, we get $D = 3$.

Thus:

$$\begin{array}{c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c}
 && 1 & B & C & 9 _{5} \\ 
&+& B & C & 9 & 1 _{5} \\ 
\cline{2-6} 
&0 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 2 _{5}. \\ 
\end{array}$$

Gives us:

$$\begin{array}{c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c}
 && 1 & B & C & 9 _{5} \\ 
&+& B & C & 9 & 1 _{5} \\ 
\cline{2-6} 
&0 & 0 & 4 & 1 _{5}. \\ 
\end{array}$$

Which would be:

$$\begin{array}{c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c@{}c}
 && 1 & B & C & 9 _{5} \\ 
&+& B & C & 9 & 0 _{5} \\ 
\cline{2-6} 
&0 & 0 & 4 & 1 _{5}. \\ 
\end{array}$$
